appraisal_events.evidence: « Comme il ressemble à sa mère » ... « Ce petit jeune homme a ses beaux yeux et aussi ça », dit-elle, en traçant avec son doigt une ligne sur le bas de son front.
appraisal_events.explanation: La dame en rose (Odette) warmly admires the boy, remarking on his resemblance to his parents and praising his eyes, directing affectionate attention toward him.

appraisal_events.evidence: « ...dit vivement mon oncle d'un ton bourru » ; « ...grogna mon oncle qui ne se souciait pas plus de faire des présentations à distance en disant le nom de maman que d'en faire de près. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's characterization of the uncle's brusque tone, growled replies, and reluctance to make even a distant introduction exposes his social discomfort and evasiveness in this exchange.

status_effects.explanation: The boy is admired for his appearance and resemblance to his parents, a mild positive local appraisal.
His gruff, growled responses and reluctance to make formal introductions position him as evasive and ill at ease in the conversation.
By contrast with the uncle's brusqueness, Odette's precise, gracious corrections and warm attention give her the more composed and assured position in the exchange.

ambiguities: The narrator's description of the uncle's gruff, growling manner ('grogna', 'd'un ton bourru') could be read either as narrator-endorsed characterization or as comparatively neutral reporting of dialogue tags, affecting how strongly the diminishment should be weighted.
